title: Material Safety Data Sheet
description: Free Material Safety Data Sheet template for construction you can edit online and download as PDF. Covers section 1: identification, section 2: hazards identification, section 3: composition.
html:
Section 1: Identification

Product Name: Asphalt (Hot Mix/ Roofing) Synonyms: Bitumen, Blacktop, Asphalt Cement

CAS Number: 8052-42-4 Use: Paving, Roofing, Waterproofing

Manufacturer: ______________ Emergency Phone: ______________ Date: ______________

Section 2: Hazards Identification

GHS PICTOGRAMS: [GHS02] [GHS08] [GHS07]

SIGNAL WORD: WARNING

HAZARD STATEMENTS:

• H226: Flammable liquid and vapor (if heated) • H315: Causes skin irritation

• H317: May cause allergic skin reaction • H335: May cause respiratory irritation

• H350: May cause cancer (if contains PAHs) • H304: May be fatal if swallowed (hot)

PRECAUTIONARY STATEMENTS:

• P210: Keep away from heat/sparks/open flames • P280: Wear protective gloves/eye protection

• P301+P310: IF SWALLOWED (hot): Immediately call poison center • P302+P352: IF ON SKIN: Wash with soap/water

• P304+P340: IF INHALED (fumes): Remove to fresh air • P308+P313: IF exposed: Get medical advice

Section 3: Composition

COMPONENT CAS NUMBER % WEIGHT EXPOSURE LIMIT

Asphalt (Bitumen) 8052-42-4 90-100% 5 mg/m3 (fume)

Polycyclic Aromatic HCs Various <0.1% N/E

Hydrogen Sulfide (when heated) 7783-06-4 Trace 10 ppm

Silica (if aggregate present) 14808-60-7 Variable 0.05 mg/m3

Section 4: First Aid Measures

EYES: Flush with cool water for 15 minutes. Seek medical attention if irritation persists.

SKIN: For hot asphalt: Cool immediately with cold water. DO NOT remove adhered asphalt. Seek medical aid.

For cold asphalt: Wash with soap and water. Remove contaminated clothing.

INHALATION: Move to fresh air. Give oxygen if breathing difficult. Seek medical attention for fume exposure.

INGESTION: If hot: Medical emergency - call 911. Do NOT induce vomiting. If cold: Not applicable.

Section 5: Fire Fighting Measures

Flash Point: >230°C (446°F) Autoignition: >400°C

Suitable Extinguishing Media: Dry chemical, CO2, foam. Water fog for cooling.

Unsuitable: Direct water stream may spread fire.

Fire Fighting Procedures: Wear SCBA. Cool containers with water. Asphalt burns with dense black smoke.

Hazardous Decomposition: Hydrogen sulfide, sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, PAHs.

Section 6: Accidental Release Measures

HOT SPILL: Barricade area. Allow to cool and solidify. Remove mechanically. Do not use water on hot asphalt.

COLD SPILL: Scoop or shovel into containers. Avoid dust generation.

Environmental: Prevent entry into drains. Asphalt can coat wildlife and smother aquatic life.

Section 7: Handling And Storage

Handling Hot: Use insulated gloves and clothing. Beward of burns. Control fumes with local exhaust.

Handling Cold: Avoid dust. Use appropriate PPE.

Storage: Store away from oxidizers and heat sources. Keep containers closed.

Incompatible Materials: Strong oxidizers, chlorine compounds.

Section 8: Exposure Controls / PPE

EXPOSURE LIMITS:

• Asphalt fumes: OSHA PEL 5 mg/m3 (8-hr TWA), ACGIH TLV 0.5 mg/m3 (benzene-soluble aerosol)

• Hydrogen Sulfide: OSHA PEL 20 ppm ceiling, 50 ppm 10-min peak

ENGINEERING CONTROLS: Local exhaust ventilation for hot work. Enclosed pavers. Fume extraction systems.

PPE:

• Eyes: Safety glasses with side shields. Face shield if splashing possible.

• Skin (hot): Heat-resistant gloves (leather/ Kevlar), long sleeves, full-length pants, steel-toe boots.

• Skin (cold): Chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile), work clothing.

• Respiratory: Organic vapor respirator for fumes. N95 for dust. SCBA for confined spaces.

• Thermal protection: When handling hot material.

Section 9: Physical And Chemical Properties

Appearance (Hot): Black viscous liquid Odor: Strong, characteristic pH: Neutral

Appearance (Cold): Black semi-solid Softening Point: 35-70°C Flash Point: >230°C

Specific Gravity: 1.0-1.1 Solubility: Insoluble in water Vapor Pressure: Very low

Boiling Point: >300°C VOC Content: <0.5% (typical)

Section 10: Stability And Reactivity

Stability: Stable under normal conditions.

Reactivity: Not reactive with water. Can react with strong oxidizers.

Conditions to Avoid: Excessive heat (generates fumes). Open flames.

Hazardous Decomposition: Fumes when heated - H2S, SO2, CO, PAHs, smoke.

Section 11: Toxicological Information

Acute Effects: Hot material causes severe thermal burns. Fumes cause eye/throat irritation, headache, nausea.

Chronic Effects: Prolonged fume exposure may cause respiratory issues. Skin sensitization possible.

Carcinogenicity: IARC Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic) for asphalt fumes. PAHs may be carcinogenic.

Target Organs: Skin, respiratory system, eyes.

Sections 12-16: Regulatory & Other Info

Disposal: Dispose in accordance with local regulations. Can be recycled.

Transport: Not regulated (DOT) when cold. Hot asphalt may require special handling.

Regulatory: OSHA HazCom - Hazardous. SARA 311/312 - Fire, Acute, Chronic.

California Prop 65: Contains chemicals known to cause cancer (PAHs).

HMIS: Health: 2* Flammability: 1 Physical: 0 NFPA: Health: 2 Fire: 1 Reactivity: 0
